To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. Preferences and ethical priorities can be modeled by using data driven and logical methods; 2. The two methods can be combined in the same system to model the interaction between preferences and ethical priorities; 3. The combination of preferences and ethical priorities can serve as a general model of thinking fast and slowly in AI.

(i) we can use preferences and ethical priorities to design machines with degrees of personalized and ethical behavior; (ii) the combination of preferences and ethical priorities can be modeled as a two-agent system; (iii) the same system can be used to design machines that exhibit different degrees of fast and slow thinking; (iv) we can use data-driven and symbolic methods to model and combine preferences and ethical priorities
we can model preferences and ethical priority using symbolic or data driven methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of intelligent agents that are capable of combining both data driven and logic based reasoning, to model preferences and to reason about ethical priorities.
the design of AI systems that combine data driven and symbolic approaches to modeling preferences, ethical priorities, and human's thinking fast and slow.
designing AI agents that are both personalized and ethical, and we propose two different approaches to achieve this.

the two approaches described in this paper are not in competition, and they are complementary
the future of AI is not a single AI, but a set of AI agents that can be used to build a complex system.
the two approaches we present are promising, but still in their early stages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of data driven and symbolic AI can be a very powerful tool for the design of intelligent systems.
we are trying to design a machine that can be both a "good friend" and a "good lawyer" for you.
we need to think fast and slow in order to design AI systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can exploit the two different systems that humans employ to think fast and slow in AI, in order to model and reason in a personalized and ethically responsible way.
the design of future AI systems requires to combine different approaches to model and reason about preferences and ethical priorities.

we should not be scared by the prospect of machines taking over, as long as they are designed to follow human's thinking fast and slow, and as long as they do not exhibit the kind of thinking fast and sloppy that is typical of humans.
